    Everyone has that traveler in their life. That person who feels more at home on a 14-hour train ride than a quiet Sunday on the couch. They speak multiple languages, have a gut like a goat, and make friends wherever they go. Whether they’re your kindred spirit or the person you live vicariously through, one thing never changes: They always need latest gear.

    That’s what makes travelers so fun to buy for. But you don’t want to get them just anything. The key is to find that clever gift even they didn’t know they needed, and that’s where we come in. From streaming gadgets for the hotel to portable espresso makers and high-capacity chargers, these are our favorite gifts to help travelers take their next adventure to the next level.

    Give Yourself A Gift With Holiday Travel Deals. Make the most of the season with limited-time holiday offers on travel and more. However you choose to celebrate, explore more ways to save and make your next journey even more rewarding. Terms apply. Ends December 15, 2026.

    Every traveler needs a go-to backpack, and the Uniqlo Utility stands out for all the little things. Its minimalist, water-resistant design hides plenty of pockets on the front and sides, plus a roomy laptop sleeve and extras, including a handy key holder in the front pocket.

    It has been revealed that few things are more frustrating on a long flight than trying to keep your phone stable between your seasoned pretzels and fellow passengers. Thankfully, MiiKare’s adjustable, inexpensive clamp can make things less stressful for your favorite frequent flyer, so they can finally watch Olympus Has Fallen in peace.

    In a recent development, we all tend to skimp on simple items for ourselves, which is why this fancy-pants sleep mask makes such a thoughtful present. Its 3D contoured fit is designed to block all light while providing plush memory foam comfort so your loved one can get the rest they need between adventures.

    According to recent reports, for frequent flyers, a plain suitcase sticker may not be enough. In the age of QR codes, Pebblebee’s Link Bag Tags make a lot more sense. They’re battery-free, scannable by anyone with a phone, and offer built-in privacy with the ability to share or deny personal information.

    Sources indicate that they say once you go bidet, you never go back. That’s certainly harder to achieve when traveling outside Japan, though Tushy offers an effective solution with its handy, collapsible bidet. The manual contraption isn’t heated, but one portable bathroom luxury at a time.

    It has been revealed that mechanism’s clever, durable creations are a favorite here at The Verge. The organization’s foldable tray table mount is particularly brilliant, offering travelers an ergonomic way to mount devices — including larger gaming handhelds like the Steam Deck — for easy access on long flights. Just don’t forget to pick up the proper grip.

    Built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

    What if you could give the gift of stress-free Wi-Fi on the go? That’s the promise of TP-Link’s dual-band Roam 7, a portable Wi-Fi 7 router that simplifies connecting to public portals so travelers can connect everything to a single device and be done with it.

    Industry observers note that for the fastidious person on your list who can’t stop polishing their camera, tablet, or other delicate piece of equipment, there’s the lightweight Magic Wrap. The foldable, plush fabric sticks to itself, with no zippers, edges, or even magnets to scuff or scratch your most precious gear.

    You can’t project anything anywhere from your phone or watch (yet), but the Aurzen Zip makes that moment feel closer. Bright and durable, the foldable projector can mirror content from your phone or tablet on most flat surfaces, but fair warning: It doesn’t work with streaming services like Netflix without a $129.99 CastPlay HDMI dongle.

    Whether your favorite traveler is a packing nerd or a slob who’s always losing everything (we’re not here to judge), everyone can use a little extra organization. Cocoon’s Grid-It accessories store it all, from chargers and gadgets to makeup and passports, with flexible straps to lock it all in.

    According to recent reports, losing important documents on a trip can be disastrous. Bagsmart’s Blast Travel Pouch is a great way to keep them all safe, with multiple pockets, an easily adjustable strap, and even RFID blocking to deflect electronic thieves.

    It’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

    Sources indicate that one charging port, two phones. That’s not a problem with Anker’s dual-headed USB-C cable, which offers either 4 or 6 feet of length to provide game-changing versatility when you need it most.

    Who notes you can’t travel with a big screen? The Xreal One Pro feature dual micro-OLED displays to project a virtual 171-inch screen from your device of choice. A 57-degree field of view, max 120Hz refresh rate, and built-in speakers round things out, delivering portable cinematic entertainment for one.

    In a recent development, apple’s AirPods Pro are the epitome of wireless earbud refinement, with fantastic noise-canceling and transparency modes, a light and airy fit, and clear sound thanks to ear tips that seal your ears without plugging them up. The latest pair continues the quest for perfection with faster processing, more features, and better ergonomics than ever.

    Oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness-tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

    According to recent reports, whether you’re white-water rafting or trekking through a damp jungle, keeping your gear dry is essential. The Sea to Summit dry bag is a slick, affordable solution with clever features, including a reflective interior and a D-ring buckle to secure it to boats and bikes. The solid warranty is just a plus.

    Sources indicate that switchBot’s powerful, battery-powered fan is a substantial upgrade over your average plug-in. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. You can also control it via an app, and it even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

    Recent findings suggest that espresso in the woods? Yes, please. The GR2’s magical mechanics make it possible, letting you turn 12 ounces of grounds into espresso without power. Its carrying case houses all the accessories needed to get that sweet shot of bean, making real coffee available virtually anywhere.

    Theragun’s latest therapeutic cure for sore muscles is as packable as it is luxurious. The third-gen Mini includes clever features like a travel lock to keep it off during transport, guided routines, and USB-C charging. There’s even a Y2K edition for the ’90s kid in all of us.

    For travelers hitting the road when the thermometer is rising, cooling off is essential. Nitecore’s long-lasting izzCool 10 Pro offers heat relief with a powerful fan and fillable reservoir that mists you for a refreshing respite from the sun. It even works with larger containers to double as a nighttime humidifier.

    Every traveler needs quality noise-canceling for long flights, but flagship headphones are becoming increasingly spendy. Sony’s former flagship WH-1000XM4 were so good, they’ve been bestsellers through two new generations. Now the company has revamped them in the XM4C, adding minor improvements to a stone-cold classic at a nice price.

    Packing light is essential for all travelers, but it’s particularly vital for those who trek long distances. This high-capacity Nitecore charger is a killer addition to any pack, with water resistance, fast charging, and a slim, lightweight design that can power your devices without weighing them down.

    The Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most important trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

    Industry observers note that every traveler’s been there. You get to the hotel or rental place, go to plug in your gear, and there’s only one outlet available. Fortunately, Tessan’s pack-friendly power strip offers all the ports, with multiple USB-C, USB-A, and AC inputs to charge everything in one place.

    If you have an avid road tripper on your list, Ugreen’s four-port car charger blends slick design with serious utility. More importantly, it has a built-in retractable USB-C cable that delivers up to 60W of power and keeps things tidy.

    It has been revealed that for on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

    Buying your loved one a pair of shoes is tougher than you might think, but a gift card to The Walking Manufacturer is a step in the right direction. The store offers a wide variety of ultra-comfortable kicks, boots, sandals, and even orthotics, along with a shoe finder to help them find the right fit.

    It has been revealed that retroid has had its stumbles, but the Pocket 5 is a hit, making it a great gift for the globe-trotting gamer. With a 5.5-inch OLED screen, a light yet durable design, and tons of titles available from the Google Play Store, the portable deck provides plenty of reasons to keep playing through the runway taxi.

    In a recent development, if you have a friend who constantly complains about their partner’s snoring habits, Soundcore’s Sleep A30 could be a gift they’ll never forget. With a comfy design, even for side sleepers, and advanced noise-canceling tech that actively adjusts to mask unwanted sounds, they’re a recipe for sweet, silent relief.

    Latest parents need everything, all at once, and traveling always raises the stakes. The Hatch Go is the sound machine they’ll be thanking you for well into toddlerhood. Offering 10 soothing sounds from a crazy-compact frame with up to 15 hours of juice, it’s simple, effective, and essential.

    Recent findings suggest that how is your giftee supposed to bring you back something special when they’re already overpacked? The Matador Packable Duffel, of course. The durable, 30-liter carrier breaks down to micro size, then easily expands to hold loads of overseas paraphernalia. It’s a win-win!

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its people.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿.

    Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿.

    Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that’s designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its people. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.

    According to recent reports, first spotted by Patentlyze, the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers.

    According to the patent, My Channel would be able to churn out entire movies of various genres. If a user watches a lot of videos about Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, the system might serve up something like Ash Koosha’s Odysseus: The Fall. The patent details how My Channel might be able to connect to other streaming services — which would give it even more information about users and, presumably, access to useful training data for video generation. It all seems like a convoluted way to whip up AI knockoffs of professionally produced art, but what’s most unsettling about the patent are its mentions of My Channel creating digital avatars of users and turning them into “the protagonist or lead character” in the content it pumps out.

    According to recent reports, setting aside the fact that My Channel would use photos, videos, and audio clips of people to create these avatars, the system sounds like it is designed to generate a form of “entertainment” that is deeply at odds with what makes engaging with art a worthwhile, enjoyable experience. It can be fun to metaphorically project one’s self into fictional narratives to understand how characters feel, but what Google is proposing is giving people access to an endless supply of bespoke content that doesn’t at all encourage them to use their imaginations to empathize with or relate to the characters. The patent makes it seem like Google thinks that viewers would be entertained enough just by seeing themselves onscreen. That’s bleak in and of itself because My Channel sounds very much like an unholy cross between JibJab and the panoptic elements of Google.

    My Channel feels like an even more depressing idea when you consider how the service would make it that much easier for its users to avoid broadening their horizons by being exposed to latest things that exist outside their comfort zones. If Google were able to strike the right licensing deals with other streaming services, My Channel users could presumably gorge themselves on artless AI regurgitations of preexisting content. That might keep some people glued to the service — a goal that every streaming platform strives for — but it would also discourage them from engaging with entertainment that isn’t expressly crafted to appeal to their assumed tastes.

    When people refer to AI-generated videos as “slop,” they’re talking about the fact that generative models are incapable of generating art with the same kind of creative intention that makes human-made stories compelling. Video generation models can mimic visual elements of the data (read: movies and series) they’re trained on, but they cannot truly think or feel in the way that directors, writers, and actors can. This reality is why it has been so baffling to see AI-boosting entertainment companies, streamers, and studios insisting that the technology will fundamentally revolutionize the industry for the better. It feels much more likely that gen AI is going to keep flooding the internet with garbage no one wants to watch.

    South London Gallery director Margot Heller to leave role after 25 years

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Margot Heller, the director of the South London Gallery, will step down from her position in May 2027 after more than 25 years.
    • In a recent development, heller, who joined SLG in 2001, plans to become an independent curator and adviser.
    • “After 25 years at the helm, I feel it’s time for newly introduced adventures in my career,” Heller stated in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Margot Heller, the director of the South London Gallery, will step down from her position in May 2027 after more than 25 years. Over this time the institution’s physical footprint has more than tripled and visitor numbers increased tenfold, according to a gallery statement.

    In a recent development, heller, who joined SLG in 2001, plans to become an independent curator and adviser. She will retain a connection with the gallery, curating the Dutch artist’s Mark Manders’s first solo exhibition at a London institution, opening at SLG on 23 September 2027.

    “After 25 years at the helm, I feel it’s time for newly introduced adventures in my career,” Heller stated in a statement.

    “From the day I took up the role, I saw an opportunity to build an institution that could be internationally acclaimed for its contemporary art programme, and deeply embedded in its local community. I have stayed true to that vision ever since.”.

    Serge Ramin, the chair of the gallery’s trustees, described Heller as “a visionary curator and cultural leader”, adding: “She leaves a museum that is artistically ambitious, rooted in its community and physically transformed.”.

    Heller’s tenure encompassed two major building projects with 6a architects: the conversion of a neighbouring house and construction of an education studio in 2010, followed by the opening of the former Peckham Road Fire Station in 2018.

    The fire station was donated in 2014 by the artist Raqib Shaw, whose identity was initially withheld. Its conversion cost £4m. Heller told The Art Newspaper in 2018 that the gallery had not been actively seeking to expand when the building was offered.

    A garden designed by Gabriel Orozco opened in 2016, while Art Block, the gallery’s free space for children and young people on the neighbouring Sceaux Gardens estate, opened at its current site in 2017.

    The artist and SLG trustee Alvaro Barrington noted: “In Margot’s time at the South London Gallery she has created pivotal moments in many artists’ careers, including my own.”.

    He added: “Her commissioning of the Orozco Garden should be considered one of the most vital architectural interventions in the UK.”.

    Exhibitions Heller has worked on during her tenure include solo presentations by Steve McQueen, Rashid Johnson, Oscar Murillo, Michael Armitage and Christina Quarles. The gallery was a joint winner of Art Fund’s Museum of the Year award in 2020.

    Industry observers note that before joining the SLG, Heller worked at Southampton City Art Gallery, becoming its director, and as director of exhibitions at Anthony d’Offay Gallery. She was appointed OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) in 2014.

    The gallery became an independent charity in 2003, having previously been managed by Southwark Council.

    Joy Gregory, an artist and SLG trustee, noted of Heller in a statement: “As a local resident and artist, I am enormously grateful for the extraordinary legacy she leaves behind and excited to see what she does next.”.

    Not Mayo Or Butter: Grilled Cheese Is Even Tastier With One Creamy Store-Bought Ingredient

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • A classic grilled cheese is a thing of both beauty and comfort.
    • It has been revealed that when spread onto the bread and covered in cheese, then warmed through in a hot pan, caramelized onion dip brings a burst of flavor and a compelling texture to the sandwich.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    A classic grilled cheese is a thing of both beauty and comfort. And of course, a simple sandwich such as this is open to interpretation, with many putting their own spin on it, like making it Swiss-style with raclette cheese or switching up the grilling process by using an air fryer, like Ree Drummond. But there's an easy addition you can make to your next grilled cheese that will make it even tastier (and it's not mayo or butter, though you can certainly use either): It's store-bought caramelized onion dip.

    It has been revealed that when spread onto the bread and covered in cheese, then warmed through in a hot pan, caramelized onion dip brings a burst of flavor and a compelling texture to the sandwich. Of course, it's definitely savory, but the caramelized onions also introduce a subtly sweet element to grilled cheese, creating a flavor sensation that is much more interesting for your taste buds. Meanwhile, the dip melts into the cheese, adding to the creaminess, while the onions introduce a little toothsome variety to chew on, beyond the softness of the filling and the crispness of the bread.

    Trader Joe's Caramelized Onion Dip is one great store-bought option, and it's part of the store's regular lineup, so you should be able to find it year-round (unless it has sold out). Whole Foods also sells a version under its 365 brand, which Amazon Prime members can shop for on Amazon.

    If you have the desire to take things a step further, you might try a mix-in or two that can elevate the taste of the dip (and therefore, your entire sandwich). That might include some dried cranberries, which can help draw out the aforementioned sweetness of the onions, creating an even bolder contrast in your salty grilled cheese. You also might play to the richness and crumble up some crisp bacon into the base. Or enhance the savory, aromatic vibes by adding both thinly sliced scallions and chives.

    Now, if you're having trouble finding caramelized onion dip at your grocery store, you could always make your own, though cooking down the onions properly can be laborious. If standing over your stove for 45 minutes doesn't appeal to you, Ina Garten cuts down on the time by using a larger pot, which allows the onions to cook more evenly and efficiently. But if you'd rather skip the cooking altogether, you might find the adjacent caramelized onion jam on store shelves. This won't be as creamy as the dip, but it will still impart that same rich, savory, and slightly sweet flavor, so it's a decent substitution.

    #206742. One Familiar Item Of Clothing Scored Lowest for Intelligence — Can You Guess Which?

    📅 08 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (417 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Org ↗ Open Full Page

    One Familiar Item Of Clothing Scored Lowest for Intelligence — Can You Guess Which?

    📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (417 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One everyday garment came last for both perceived intelligence and trustworthiness.
    • One everyday garment came last for both perceived intelligence and trustworthiness.
    • Track pants, also known as tracksuit bottoms, receive the lower ratings for perceived intelligence compared with blouses, ordinary trousers or long skirts in a study of women’s clothing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One everyday garment came last for both perceived intelligence and trustworthiness.

    One everyday garment came last for both perceived intelligence and trustworthiness.

    Track pants, also known as tracksuit bottoms, receive the lower ratings for perceived intelligence compared with blouses, ordinary trousers or long skirts in a study of women’s clothing.

    Of the six types of clothing the researchers compared, track pants also received the lowest average ratings for trustworthiness.

    Blouses topped the rankings for intelligence and trustworthiness but scored near the bottom for confidence.

    Short skirts demonstrated almost the reverse pattern, scoring near the top for confidence and lower than long skirts on both intelligence and trustworthiness.

    Short skirts also gave the strongest impression of sexual interest, showing how much people can read into a hemline.

    Long skirts fell between short skirts and blouses on confidence, while ordinary trousers scored higher than tracksuit bottoms on both intelligence and trustworthiness.

    Onesies gave the strongest impression of happiness and scored about as high as short skirts for confidence.

    White clothes suggested a happier wearer than grey clothes did, with black clothes coming last.

    These examples show how the impression changes with the question being asked: a blouse came out ahead for intelligence, while a onesie came out ahead for happiness.

    The researchers began by asking about 200 people what they thought clothes could tell them about someone and comparing their answers with traits examined in previous research.

    They then gathered ratings on 5,000 photographs from online shops, covering five kinds of impressions: intelligence, confidence, trustworthiness, happiness and sexual interest.

    Participants formed these impressions from photographs of the garments alone, without seeing anyone wearing them.

    The results highlighted that who was doing the judging explained more of the variation in ratings than which garment they saw.

    For example, one person might associate tracksuit bottoms with training for a race, while another might picture someone spending a Sunday on the sofa.

    The researchers draw a parallel between judging people by their clothes and judging them by their faces:.

    “That is, much like inferences from faces, the inferred attributes often lie in the eye of the beholder.”.

    The study was published in the Journal of Computational Social Science (Rosenbusch et al., 2021).

    The $30,000 average wedding figure you see everywhere is misleading. That number is skewed upward by luxury weddings in expensive metros like Latest York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. The national median — the number where half of weddings cost more and half cost less — sits closer to $10,000 to $15,000. That distinction matters because it means a beautiful, memorable wedding is absolutely possible without spending five figures you do not have.

    The FI perspective adds another layer: every dollar spent on a wedding is a dollar that cannot compound for decades. A $30,000 wedding invested for 30 years at a 7% average annual return grows to roughly $228,000. That does not mean you should elope in a courthouse (unless you want to), but it does mean you should spend intentionally on the categories that matter most to you and cut ruthlessly everywhere else.

    Here is where the typical wedding dollar goes:.

    Industry observers note that the biggest takeaway from this table: venue and catering are 60-70% of the total. If you can reduce those two categories, you change the entire math.

    Not all wedding spending creates equal memories. Research consistently indicates that couples remember three things most vividly years later: the ceremony itself, the food and drinks, and the photographs. Almost nobody remembers the chair covers, the napkin folds, or the custom monogram on the cocktail napkins.

    That insight creates a clear FI-aligned strategy: splurge on what creates lasting memories (photographer, food, music) and minimize everything else.

    Industry observers note that the golden rule of wedding budgeting: if you cannot remember whether a detail was present at the last three weddings you attended, your guests will not notice either. Cut it without guilt.

    The biggest financial mistake couples make is not setting a firm budget before visiting any vendors. Venues and vendors are skilled at upselling, and without a hard number in mind, costs spiral swiftly. Start with a number you can pay in cash — wedding debt is one of the worst ways to begin a marriage and a direct threat to your FI timeline.

    Follow this payment timeline to manage cash flow without credit card debt:.

    A practical savings strategy: divide your total budget by the number of months until the wedding and automate that transfer to a dedicated savings account. If your budget is $15,000 and your wedding is 15 months away, that is $1,000 per month. Treat it like any other savings goal on your FI path — automate, do not touch, and watch it grow.

    According to recent reports, for couples on the FI path, consider this reframe: every dollar you shave from the wedding budget is a dollar that starts compounding immediately. Cutting $5,000 from a $20,000 wedding and investing that savings at 7% for 25 years creates roughly $27,000 in future wealth. You can have a wonderful wedding and build wealth simultaneously — but only if you blueprint intentionally from the start.

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Before finalizing your wedding budget, run the compound interest math on any amount you are considering spending. A $30,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $228,000. A $15,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $114,000. This is not an argument against celebrating — it is an argument for spending intentionally on what matters to you and cutting everything else. The couple who spends $15,000 on a joyful celebration and invests the other $15,000 gets both the wedding and a significant head start on financial independence.

Some venues offer discounts of 40% or more for weekday weddings (Monday through Thursday). Off-season months like January, February, March, and November also offer significant savings.

    It has been revealed that tips for vendors (plan 15-20% for catering staff, bartenders, and drivers), alterations for wedding attire ($200-$500), marriage license fees ($30-$100), and overtime charges if the reception runs past the contracted time. Build a 10% contingency buffer into your total budget for these surprises.

    Sources indicate that set your budget privately as a couple before discussing with family. Present it as a decision, not a discussion. If family members want upgrades, they are welcome to fund those specific additions. Protect your financial foundation — the marriage matters more than the wedding, and starting debt-free sets up your partnership for success.

    It has been revealed that A meaningful wedding does not require $30,000 or any specific dollar amount. Set a cash budget based on what you can afford without debt, allocate spending toward what creates lasting memories (food, photography, people), and cut everything else. Every dollar you save on the wedding is a dollar that starts compounding toward your financial independence. The couples with the strongest financial futures are the ones who celebrate joyfully within their means and invest the difference.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Sources indicate that yogurt's contained lactic acid functions as a mild, but nevertheless efficient, tenderizer, lightly marinating the meat.
    • Recent findings suggest that and if you use Greek yogurt for the task, you'll get a nice dose of added protein, too.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that incorporating secret ingredients into your burger patties elevates the dish in unexpected ways. Some components flavor the meat while others enhance the texture. For an add-in that does both — with a delicious underlying creaminess — look no further than yogurt. The dairy works as a ground beef tenderizer, making a burger that's softer and full of moisture. Not to mention, yogurt is an effective enhancement in chicken or turkey patties, too.

    Sources indicate that yogurt's contained lactic acid functions as a mild, but nevertheless efficient, tenderizer, lightly marinating the meat. The inclusion of a liquid naturally adds lots of moisture to a burger — you certainly won't have to worry about a disappointingly dry result. Plus, the ingredient lends the burger a lightly creamy mouthfeel.

    Recent findings suggest that and if you use Greek yogurt for the task, you'll get a nice dose of added protein, too. Mix in a quarter cup of whole milk Greek yogurt — a quantity suitable for a pound of meat — and you'll up the dish by 5.5 grams of protein. This yogurt's extra fat content will further prevent dryness, all while forming a patty that's not too loose, making a burger rendition that stands out.

    Sources indicate that working yogurt into your beef patties doesn't require any special technique. You can simply stir the dairy with the beef in a bowl, seasoning with salt and pepper in parallel. Follow by forming the patties as usual, then lightly brush the exterior with oil to prevent unwanted adhesion. Prepare the yogurt burgers using your preferred method, whether you're fond of using a skillet or grilling burgers like a pro. However, if you notice your mixture appears too wet, consider adding a binder — chia seeds are a fantastic option to absorb moisture but keep things tender and juicy; panko breadcrumbs will also absorb excess liquid while keeping the bite of each burger soft.

    Such a burger tastes delicious with classic seasonings, but don't rule out creative modifications, too. The pairing of yogurt and beef recalls Greek and Middle Eastern cuisine, so consider integrating Eastern Mediterranean seasonings into the build.

    A Greek burger spin could fold in oregano, lemon, and feta — core flavors of a Greek salad. A kofta-style patty might up the spice, working in earthy cumin, a dash of spicy harissa, and grated garlic into the mix. Alternatively, season the meat in a sweet direction by using simply turmeric and onions; the ingredients will set you up for a wide array of flavorful condiments. Build out the meal with an aromatic herbal yogurt sauce, a bold dose of roasted peppers, or a marinated arugula salad, and you'll make a burger rendition that'll become a frequent part of the rotation.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theartnewspaper ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: UK government places export ban on Mughal calligraphy works valued at £900,000

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (399 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The UK government has temporarily blocked two 16th-century volumes of Mughal calligraphy from being taken out of the country permanently.
    • The export bar, which allows time for a UK gallery or institution to acquire the calligraphy works, will initially expire on 15 February 2027, after which the owners will have 15 business days to consider any offers at the recommended price of £900,000, followed by a second deferral period of four months.
    • In a recent development, “By keeping the volumes in the country, it is hoped researchers can study how the construction of such calligraphic collections has evolved.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The UK government has temporarily blocked two 16th-century volumes of Mughal calligraphy from being taken out of the country permanently.

    The export bar, which allows time for a UK gallery or institution to acquire the calligraphy works, will initially expire on 15 February 2027, after which the owners will have 15 business days to consider any offers at the recommended price of £900,000, followed by a second deferral period of four months.

    In a recent development, “By keeping the volumes in the country, it is hoped researchers can study how the construction of such calligraphic collections has evolved. Given so few works of this kind survive intact, its preservation makes it especially valuable,” indicates a statement from the UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS). The volumes were kept in a private collection from the 1980s until 2020 when they were sold at Sotheby’s London for £620,000 (before fees) to a specialist dealer in London.

    The calligraphic works, thought to be over 400 years old, are spread across 29 leaves and feature gold ornamentation of plant and animal motifs. The two volumes derive from an imperial album created around 1595-1605.

    Sources indicate that according to the DCMS statement, the original album was prepared for Mughal Emperor Akbar or his son Prince Salim at the royal workshop either in Lahore or Agra. Muhammad Hussain Kashmiri and Abd al-Rahim al-Haravi are among the calligraphers featured.

    The Black Prince marble bust by Michael Rysbrack (around 1735).

    Courtesy Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile another export bar has been placed on a marble bust of the 14th-century prince Edward of Woodstock, the son of King Edward III of England and popularly known as the Black Prince. Created around 1735, the sculpture was made by the Flemish sculptor, Michael Rysbrack.

    This export bar will initially expire on 5 February 2027, after which the owners will have 15 business days to consider any offers at the recommended price of £496,044 plus VAT, followed by a second deferral period of four months.

    Fiona Twycross, the heritage minister, claims in a statement: “For nearly three hundred years [the sculpture] has shaped how we tell the story of our medieval history and I hope that in a public gallery in the UK it can tell that story much more powerfully for many more years to come.”.

    It has been revealed that when you need a side to go along with your main dinner entree and you need one fast, it's reassuring to know that shelf-stable, pantry-sitting canned goods have got your back. Included in Food Republic's list of inexpensive canned foods you'll use all the time are beans, and along with the plain black or red varieties (which typically need to be combined with other ingredients to make a reasonable side), you could also reach for scrumptious, creamy baked beans. But while they're totally fine heated up straight from the can, they can certainly benefit from a drizzle of molasses.

    Molasses might not be the first thing you think of when you consider add-ins, but many homemade recipes call for it, and for good reason. Made by boiling down sugarcane juice or refining sugar, the rich, thick syrup is slightly smoky and sweet, with robust, burnt caramel notes, making it a perfect match for deepening the flavor of sometimes weak-tasting canned baked beans and bringing them closer to homemade.

    It is for this reason that molasses is also preferable to honey here. Honey is intensely sweet, can taste almost floral at times, and has a delicate flavor, whereas molasses is bolder and has a meatier taste that can make its presence known among the other ingredients in the dish.

    It's important to note that there are three main types of molasses: light, dark, and blackstrap, and they each have different flavor profiles. For canned baked beans, you'll likely want to stick with light or dark because blackstrap is intensely bitter (also, light is the sweetest of the three, so if sweetness is important to you, go with that one). If you're heating the beans on the stove, you can start by drizzling in about half a tablespoon of molasses per 28-ounce can, bringing the mixture to a boil, and then simmering for about 10 minutes. If you're baking them, likewise, just stir in the molasses before putting the dish in the oven — it couldn't be simpler.

    If you don't have any molasses sitting about, don't panic. There are plenty of other additions that can help upgrade canned baked beans and make them taste less, well, pantry-fied. Take brown sugar, for example — did you know that it's often just white sugar and molasses combined? A little bit will still bring that sweet contrast to balance out the savory flavors and give you a deeper, more complex finish.

    According to recent reports, another great option is one you might normally use on your pancakes: maple syrup. You don't want to use the fake stuff that's primarily made of corn syrup and artificial flavors and colors, but rather 100% real Grade A maple syrup for the best flavor. Its sweetness again deliciously contrasts with and enhances the canned baked beans' savoriness, while the maple flavor adds its unique caramelly, toffee-like notes to the dish.

    2 Personality Traits Are Linked to Lower Inflammation

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lower inflammation is associated with less fatigue, a lower risk of depression and a slower decline in reasoning as people age.
    • Lower inflammation is associated with less fatigue, a lower risk of depression and a slower decline in reasoning as people age.
    • People who score higher in conscientiousness or extraversion tend to have lower levels of certain markers of inflammation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lower inflammation is associated with less fatigue, a lower risk of depression and a slower decline in reasoning as people age.

    Lower inflammation is associated with less fatigue, a lower risk of depression and a slower decline in reasoning as people age.

    People who score higher in conscientiousness or extraversion tend to have lower levels of certain markers of inflammation.

    Among the qualities that make up conscientiousness, being hardworking and organised stood out.

    For extraversion, which includes both sociability and energy, the clearest result was for people who described themselves as active.

    These patterns matter because inflammation that stays elevated over time is linked to both physical and psychological health.

    Lower levels of long-term inflammation are linked to a lower risk of heart disease, stroke and premature death.

    They have also been associated with less fatigue, a lower risk of depression and a slower decline in reasoning as people age.

    The researchers pooled data from six studies involving more than 19,000 adults in the United States, England and Japan.

    Participants rated how well words such as ‘organised’, ‘hardworking’ and ‘active’ described them.

    The researchers then looked at how those answers related to two markers of inflammation in blood samples, C-reactive protein and interleukin-6.

    Earlier research had already linked higher conscientiousness with lower levels of both inflammatory markers (Luchetti et al., 2014).

    In this study, people who described themselves as organised or hardworking tended to have lower levels of both markers.

    Being hardworking highlighted the strongest association within conscientiousness, even stronger than the association for the overall trait score.

    People who scored higher on extraversion tended to have lower C-reactive protein, and much of that association came from how active they said they were.

    In fact, being active was more strongly associated with lower C-reactive protein than any other characteristic the researchers examined.

    Being talkative showed a small association in the opposite direction, while being lively was associated with lower levels of both inflammatory markers.

    In several of the studies, the association with being active held up even after the researchers took other aspects of extraversion into account.

    Being active and hardworking may both reflect how much energy people have for everyday tasks.

    In earlier research, people who scored higher on the activity aspect of extraversion or the achievement-striving aspect of conscientiousness tended to have better aerobic capacity during a brisk walking test (Terracciano et al., 2013).

    Regular physical activity could help explain part of the association with inflammation.

    The relationship could run in the other direction, too, if people with higher inflammation feel less energetic and come to see themselves as less active or lively.

    The study was published in the journal Psychoneuroendocrinology (Stephan et al., 2026).

    Sources indicate that psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004.     • Industry observers note that easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Industry observers note that think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind. However, bread-based dishes are widely enjoyed in the East Asian country, both in cafes and as street food. An especially popular breakfast rendition is gilgeori toast, a comforting breakfast sandwich stuffed with eggs and shredded vegetables.

    Industry observers note that easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation. Traditionally, this sandwich calls for a fluffy loaf of milk or brioche bread, the buttery soft texture turning crisp on the outside once toasted. Meanwhile, the filling comprises a variable shredded vegetable medley: Cabbage traditionally forms the centerpiece, joined by carrots, onions, scallions, and often garlic chives. Mixed with egg and then pan-fried into an aesthetic golden-brown patty, the filling delectably complements the soft bread. Gilgeori is usually rounded out with a sprinkle of sugar and a drizzle of ketchup and mustard.

    Industry observers note that it's an assembly that easily comes together during bleary morning hours, yet nevertheless offers a nutritious start to the day. One sandwich can pack in around six ounces of shredded cabbage, which amounts to over 4 grams of fiber. Add up the fiber from a tablespoon of carrot, two of sliced onion, and two whole green onions, and you're including another 1.5 grams. Then, add in two slices of thick-cut brioche sandwich bread, and you've got an extra 2. That's about 7.5 grams, which is around a quarter of what you need a day, already knocked out by breakfast. Mixed with the roughly 6.5 grams of protein from the egg alongside filling bread, the sandwich serves as a terrific way to start the day.

    According to recent reports, the morning isn't always the best time to precisely reconstruct a recipe. Thankfully, gilgeori toast welcomes a wide array of reinterpretations and ingredients. Starting with the bread, feel free to swap the milk bread for sourdough, whole wheat, or even a convenient store-bought whole grain like Ezekiel or Dave's Killer. You'll lose out on some of the dish's airiness, but potentially gain extra fiber content in the process. Two slices of Dave's Killer 21 Whole Grains and Seeds contain some 8 grams of fiber, more than doubling the total of the sandwich.

    Up the satiation further by adding on a slice of seared ham, a filling also enjoyed in Korea. And cheese is always welcome, whether American, cheddar, or fontina – Martha Stewart's go-to for breakfast sandwiches. Instead of the sugar sprinkle, lend the dish a sweet note by using jam: Raspberry or cherry jam makes a great fit. Not to mention, you can replace the ketchup and mustard with a condiment of your preference; you can buy a bottle of Gochujang Sriracha Hot Sauce online, for instance. The template of bread and shredded vegetables works with many flavors, perfect for morning enjoyment.

    Breaking: Not Cinnamon: Add A Pinch Of This Warm Spice To French Toast For A Flavor Boost

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that warm spices on French toast create a cozy, aromatic breakfast dish that warms your sinuses as much as your tongue.
    • In a recent development, some folks call cardamom the queen of spices — and for good reason.
    • Six pods should yield about half a teaspoon of ground spice, enough for roughly six pieces of French toast (though pod sizes vary).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that warm spices on French toast create a cozy, aromatic breakfast dish that warms your sinuses as much as your tongue. While traditional cinnamon is always a solid choice, cardamom French toast adds latest layers of fresh, almost herbal notes for something far more complex and just as compatible with your other favorite seasonings.

    In a recent development, some folks call cardamom the queen of spices — and for good reason. As flavorful as it is versatile, it's a shelf-stable ingredient that lasts a long time, grinds easily into a powder, and seems to taste amazing with just about any sweet recipe you could think of. While it can be a tad on the expensive side, small amounts suffuse your French toast with deep flavor, so even a small jar of seeds can last you quite a while. The key is to mix it with your other dried spices to create a delicate flavor profile similar to mulled drinks, festive winter desserts, and spiced ciders.

    Six pods should yield about half a teaspoon of ground spice, enough for roughly six pieces of French toast (though pod sizes vary). Since you want a smooth batter without much texture, it's best to grind the seeds into a fine powder before mixing. The moisture from eggs and milk should help protect the delicate spice, but remember that heat affects the flavor release of spices. Gently toasting the pods beforehand is a great way to bump up the flavor without using more of the pricey ingredient.

    It has been revealed that though cardamom has quite a bit of flavor, it's also rather delicate and can slip into the background or be the star of the show, depending on your preferences. In sweet dishes, there are few warm spices it pairs poorly with, and more obscure ingredients can really elevate its flavor for something showstopping.

    Just about any warming spice you'd associate with the colder months should pair beautifully with cardamom. Cinnamon is a bold counterpart that can carry most of the flavor profile without overshadowing it when used in moderation. Allspice and cloves are a match made in heaven, providing an almost berry-like warmth to counteract cardamom's cool, herbal notes. Ground or fresh ginger can add a touch of sharpness that offers quite a bit of contrast, providing a similar bite on the tongue to garlic that's far more compatible with sugary bases.

    It has been revealed that if you really want to bump up the flavor of cardamom, don't stick to just spices. Floral notes from things like dried and ground orange peels, lychee, or guava really round out your French toast without overpowering your spices. These are highly compatible with cardamom and make your breakfast taste almost like a pomander, with an incredible bouquet of aromas the second your bread hits the pan. You can also use food-safe flavoring oils instead, mixing them into your wet ingredients for greater control over how much flavor you're adding.

    #206717. New bi-national art initiative reframes stereotypes about Mexico-US border

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1280 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theartnewspaper ↗ Open Full Page

    New bi-national art initiative reframes stereotypes about Mexico-US border

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that can the “open wound” of the Mexico-US border be healed?
    • Juárez has long been associated with sensational narratives of violence.
    • Though seemingly worlds apart today, Ciudad Juárez and El Paso were one city until the Rio Grande river was established as the border between Mexico and the US in 1848.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that can the “open wound” of the Mexico-US border be healed? Sutura, a new bi-national art programme in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, and El Paso, Texas (18 November-22 November), looks beyond stereotypes of violence surrounding the Mexico-US border and explores how art might help mend the region’s many wounds, even imperfectly or temporarily. Sutura (Spanish for “suture”) brings together more than 100 artists across 20 venues, including the El Paso Museum of Art (EPMA), the Stanlee and Gerald Rubin Center for the Visual Arts and the Museo de Arte de Ciudad Juárez (MACJ), alongside independent projects and pop-up exhibitions.

    Juárez has long been associated with sensational narratives of violence. Persistent migration challenges, heightened by stricter border controls and alarming deportation measures, feminicides, the drug war and hyper-surveillance have shaped the local context. These aspects have permeated cultural production. “Endless works have explored this territory as a symbol and symptom of an apocalyptic future,” writes Willivaldo Delgadillo in his book-length essay Fabular Juárez (2020).

    Though seemingly worlds apart today, Ciudad Juárez and El Paso were one city until the Rio Grande river was established as the border between Mexico and the US in 1848. Despite tensions between their respective countries, the two cities are still connected by education, jobs and transit.

    It has been revealed that “On each side of the border, nuanced and contrasting fears and ideologies coexist, but there is also community,” Edgar Picazo Merino, Sutura’s founder and lead organiser, tells The Art Newspaper. “For all of us who live here, the border is a personal, lived experience.” Picazo founded the independent initiative Azul Arena in 2019 to support the Juárez-El Paso art scene; it established a permanent space in Juárez in 2022.

    Central to thinking about the border in the context of Sutura and more broadly is Chicana writer Gloria Anzaldúa’s 1987 metaphor of the border as an “open wound”. “The Third World grates against the first and bleeds,” Anzaldúa wrote. “And before a scab forms, it haemorrhages again, the lifeblood of two worlds merging to form a third country—a border culture.” The “open wound” concept has become commonplace in border literature, Picazo indicates, while Sutura seeks to deconstruct it: “If the border is a wound, how can the arts suture its many wounds, while opening places of reflection and interaction?”.

    Detail of Justin Favela's Mantecore (White Tiger) (2017), featured in Qué tanto es tantito, a group show on view at San Luis Contemporáneo, Ciudad Juárez Courtesy Haydee Alonso.

    Sutura builds on binational initiatives like Insite, which emerged in 1992 at the San Diego-Tijuana border and initially featured site-specific installations before changing formats. It also draws on regional ties. The Juárez-El Paso Border Biennial, launched in 2008 by the EPMA and MACJ, is right now in its eighth edition, Imagining the Border (until 2 May 2027). Co-curated by the Juárez-based curators Adriana Miramontes Olivas and Alejandro Morales, it features more than 80 works by artists based within 300 miles of El Paso and Juárez.

    According to recent reports, “A border that is always there, one that weighs heavily on our communities, rarely lets us imagine it,” Morales claims. “This edition opens that space, offering a plural and rigorous portrait of it as living territory.”.

    The Border Biennial has strived to shift perceptions. “The biennial has national relevance, moving beyond portrayals of the border as perpetually on fire, highlighting its creative richness and cultural legacies,” claims Edward Hayes Jr, the director of the EPMA, adding that the project requires overcoming diplomatic and logistical challenges. “We aim for the biennial to be a structural project for both institutions,” says Christian Diego Diego, MACJ’s director. Diego adds that over its past and current editions, the Border Biennial has featured more than 400 works by around 270 artists, “reflecting the border’s ambivalence and multiple stories”. Sutura’s programme includes visits to the biennial, reflecting dialogue with the artists, curators and venues.

    Sutura also grew from asking how a Juárez-El Paso art week might unfold. Border initiatives are gaining visibility. The fair Material, through its two-year Projects programme, has supported Azul Arena and the Juárez curatorial duo Un Dique with mentorship and free participation in its Mexico City and Guadalajara fairs. Un Dique joins Sutura by curating theexhibition Border Kaijus on border hypervigilance. Two other border cities have recently created art weeks amid growing efforts to decentralise a national scene largely centred on Mexico City: Tijuana held its second art week in July; Mexicali held its first in April.

    According to recent reports, “There is a growing scene among border Mexican cities with spaces and initiatives interacting,” notes Andres Payan Estrada, the director and chief curator of the Stanlee and Gerald Rubin Center for the Visual Arts and Sutura’s artistic strategy director. Still, he adds, Sutura is not an art week: “It is a non-commercial collaborative initiative with a strong community component.”.

    Installation view of the group show Costuras Territoriales at the Stanlee and Gerald Rubin Center for the Visual Arts at the University of Texas, El Paso Courtesy of the Stanlee and Gerald Rubin Center for the Visual Arts at the University of Texas, El Paso.

    In El Paso, institutional participation is strong. During Sutura, the Rubin Center is showing Costuras Territoriales (until 12 December), curated by Payan and featuring textile-inspired works by five women artists connected to the border, including Teresa Margolles, Tania Candiani and Juárez-based Olga Guerra. “The way in which artists explore the border has sometimes become a cliché,” Guerra states. “I intend to reflect relationality through a more poetic approach, incorporating locally found organic materials and fibres, along with reused materials.”.

    Industry observers note that independent initiatives are vital in Juárez, where conventional galleries are non-existent. Picazo’s Azul Arena, a pillar of the city’s scene, will present the exhibition En la línea, exploring the line as a metaphor for the border. The Juárez-based artist Haydee Alonso, co-founder of San Luis Contemporáneo, will curate the exhibition ¿Qué tanto es tantito? there and present a performance at Azul Arena. “My work analyses transborder relations through the body and objects, opening spaces within the complexities of living here,” claims Alonso, who crosses the border daily to teach at the University of Texas at El Paso. Both projects have received support from the Mellon Foundation, which Alonso and Picazo consider crucial to local initiatives. In El Paso, where independent spaces are relatively scarce, The Falstaff, a community-centred hybrid art space, will host exhibitions and concerts.

    Installation view ofthe group exhibiton Qué tanto es tantito, group show on view at San Luis Contemporáneo, Ciudad Juárez Courtesy Haydee Alonso.

    Recent findings suggest that sutura also supports the local scene by showcasing six El Paso and Juárez projects selected through an open call, with each project receiving $3,000 for production costs. The photography exhibition Relatos de la Frontera: Cuerpo y Espacio explores border perspectives through the body and space Another show, Tierra Suelta, presents works inspired by children of migrant families that settled in Juárez for reasons other than the “American dream”, integrating a community activation into the programme. These projects foreground local perspectives in a region often depicted by outsiders, alongside established artists—primarily Mexican and Mexican American—whose work reflects on the border.

    Recent findings suggest that picazo acknowledges the complexities of a bi-national event: not everyone can cross both ways because of visa restrictions and other complications. “The programme has parallel activities so you can experience Sutura even from one side of the border,” he says.

    Sutura speaks more of resilience than crisis, more of possibility than scarcity.“Historically, the border is explained one-dimensionally, yet a myriad of dynamics co-exist here,” Picazo states. “Sutura exists as a relational art encounter.”.
